quotes.text: Country House. 1722-1735 for Sir Robert Walpole, the first Prime Minister of Great Britain (1717-1742), in rivalry with his brother-in-law's Raynham. Reputed to have been built largely from public funds, a "house of State and Convenience" (Colen Campbell) for the "Houghton meeting" house-parties and for Walpole's picture collection here 1742-1779. Design, published by Colen Campbell in Vitruvius Britannicus III (1725), under discussion 1721, executed by Walpole's protege in the King's Works, Thomas Ripley, modified by James Gibbs, decorated by William Kent. Palladian with some Baroque references.

quotes.text: Fine Whitby stone ashlar, pantiled roofs. 3 storey 9 by 5 bay centre with 4 advanced angle towers, single storey colonnaded wings, quadrant to west, dog-leg to east.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1152645, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: to west, dog-leg to east. 2 storey 7 by 7 bay service wings with courtyards beyond.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1152645, Details, opening paragraph; this span begins mid-sentence at the start of the extract's second chunk and is quoted from where that chunk begins

quotes.text: East front has rusticated basement with plinth and first floor platband. 3 ground floor centre bays with 2 arched headed sashes and fanlight door, 1793 refacing of removed external staircase. 4 outer and 2 tower sashes with keystone heads. Piano nobile sashes with Gibbsian surrounds, and balustrade dados. Venetian windows with keystone heads to angles.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1152645, Details, east front

quotes.text: 9 second floor architrave surround sashes. Rich Ionic entablature with pulvinated frieze, cornice, balustrade, parapet with coping
quotes.page: Official list entry 1152645, Details, east front

quotes.text: Each ridge has 2 massive stacks with moulded cornices.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1152645, Details, east front and colonnades

quotes.text: Central single cube 2 storey Stone Hall lined with superbly detailed Whitby ashlar, stone and stucco carving. Architraved doors and aedicules. Antique busts on brackets, bas-reliefs and swags. Rysbrack chimney piece with caryatids, bas-relief above with bust of Walpole.
aisled hall with piers supporting vaults. Piano nobile above for "taste, expense, state and parade" (Hervey), little used in C18, has State rooms to north, private rooms to south.

note: Tranche 3, English Baroque / Palladian / Adam cluster, 5 Sep 2026. The richest external envelope in the Palladian half: three storeys, nine by five bays, four angle towers, two storey seven by seven service wings, two stacks a ridge, and a nine-window second floor -- and the register calls the whole thing 'Palladian with some Baroque references', which is a third party saying what this node's descent from the Baroque node would predict.
